title: Transcription shapes 3D chromatin organization by interacting with loop extrusion.
authors: Banigan, Edward J; Tang, Wen; van den Berg, Aafke A; Stocsits, Roman R; Wutz, Gordana; Brandao, Hugo B; Busslinger, Georg A; Peters, Jan-Michael; Mirny, Leonid A
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文通过Hi-C和聚合物模拟研究RNA聚合酶作为移动屏障与cohesin环挤压的相互作用，塑造3D染色质组织，虽涉及蛋白质-DNA互作和物理模拟，但核心是染色质结构而非TF-DNA特异性结合，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Cohesin folds mammalian interphase chromosomes by extruding the chromatin fiber into numerous loops. "Loop extrusion" can be impeded by chromatin-bound factors, such as CTCF, which generates characteristic and functional chromatin organization patterns. It has been proposed that transcription relocalizes or interferes with cohesin and that active promoters are cohesin loading sites. However, the effects of transcription on cohesin have not been reconciled with observations of active extrusion by cohesin. To determine how transcription modulates extrusion, we studied mouse cells in which we could alter cohesin abundance, dynamics, and localization by genetic "knockouts" of the cohesin regulators CTCF and Wapl. Through Hi-C experiments, we discovered intricate, cohesin-dependent contact patterns near active genes. Chromatin organization around active genes exhibited hallmarks of interactions between transcribing RNA polymerases (RNAPs) and extruding cohesins. These observations could be reproduced by polymer simulations in which RNAPs were moving barriers to extrusion that obstructed, slowed, and pushed cohesins. The simulations predicted that preferential loading of cohesin at promoters is inconsistent with our experimental data. Additional ChIP-seq experiments showed that the putative cohesin loader Nipbl is not predominantly enriched at promoters. Therefore, we propose that cohesin is not preferentially loaded at promoters and that the barrier function of RNAP accounts for cohesin accumulation at active promoters. Altogether, we find that RNAP is an extrusion barrier that is not stationary, but rather, translocates and relocalizes cohesin. Loop extrusion and transcription might interact to dynamically generate and maintain gene interactions with regulatory elements and shape functional genomic organization.
abstract_zh: 黏连蛋白通过将染色质纤维挤出成众多环状结构来折叠哺乳动物间期染色体。“环挤出”过程可被染色质结合因子（如CTCF）阻碍，从而产生特征性且功能性的染色质组织模式。已有研究提出，转录会重新定位或干扰黏连蛋白，且活性启动子是黏连蛋白的装载位点。然而，转录对黏连蛋白的影响尚未与黏连蛋白主动挤出的观察结果相协调。为确定转录如何调节挤出过程，我们研究了小鼠细胞，通过遗传“敲除”黏连蛋白调节因子CTCF和Wapl，可改变黏连蛋白的丰度、动态和定位。通过Hi-C实验，我们发现了活性基因附近复杂且依赖黏连蛋白的接触模式。活性基因周围的染色质组织表现出转录中的RNA聚合酶（RNAPs）与挤出中的黏连蛋白相互作用的特征。这些观察结果可通过聚合物模拟重现，其中RNAPs作为移动的挤出屏障，阻碍、减缓并推动黏连蛋白。模拟预测，黏连蛋白在启动子处的优先装载与我们的实验数据不一致。额外的ChIP-seq实验显示，假定的黏连蛋白装载因子Nipbl并非主要富集于启动子。因此，我们提出黏连蛋白并非优先装载于启动子，且RNAP的屏障功能解释了黏连蛋白在活性启动子处的积累。总体而言，我们发现RNAP是一种非静止的挤出屏障，而是能够移位并重新定位黏连蛋白。环挤出与转录可能相互作用，动态生成并维持基因与调控元件的相互作用，从而塑造功能性基因组组织。
